title: Why a support backlog explodes
objective: Learners see that a queue grows whenever tickets arrive faster than agents resolve them, that leftover backlog carries into the next day, and that one extra agent can flip a backlog that never clears into one that clears every night.

recommended.why: An animated queue makes tickets, waiting lines and busy agents tangible, so learners feel the backlog pile up hour by hour.

alternative.why: Seeing the queue versus reading the trend: which explains why small changes matter?

assumptions: A deterministic, illustrative model, not real support data: arrivals follow the same daily shape every day, scaled to the peak rate and a small weekday factor
Agents work every hour of the day at a steady pace (no breaks, shifts or absences)
Capacity per hour = agents × 60 ÷ handle time in minutes; every ticket takes the same handle time
The week runs Monday 00:00 to Friday 24:00 and starts with an empty queue
Backlog is counted at the end of each hour: backlog = max(0, previous backlog + arrivals − capacity)
units: arrivals and capacity: tickets per hour
checkDescription: At every hour the backlog equals max(0, previous backlog + arrivals − capacity), for both the chosen staffing and one more agent, and the reported peak and its hour match the series.

learnerPrompts.predict: Five agents handle 25 tickets an hour and the busiest hour brings 54. Will the queue be empty again by Tuesday morning?
learnerPrompts.explain: Add one agent. The capacity only rises by 5 tickets an hour, so why does the end-of-week backlog change so much?
